Q: Is there any way to recognize just one word without using a speech-to-text API in Python? A:

I think what you want to do is wake word detection or keyword spotting. In wake word detection, the goal is to trigger the output when a specified word is heard in input.

There are several good libraries to do this. For example check these ones:

https://github.com/Picovoice/porcupine (it requires access key from their website)

https://github.com/MycroftAI/mycroft-precise (It looks like its free)

Q: Get Windows cert container GUID A:

The [RSACertificateExtensions]::GetRSAPrivateKey(...) method would probably work in pwsh 7 as is... you're likely using pwsh 5.1; try listing the certs from the X509Store instead:

$store = [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Store]::new(
    [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.StoreName]::My,
    [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.StoreLocation]::CurrentUser)

$store.Open([System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.OpenFlags]::ReadOnly)
$store.Certificates |
    Where-Object HasPrivateKey |
    ForEach-Object { [System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.RSACertificateExtensions]::GetRSAPrivateKey($_) }

If this method works then I'm assuming Get-ChildItem is opening the Certs using an obsolete method incompatible with GetRSAPrivateKey(...) extension method.

Q: What are the pros and cons of the assorted Java web frameworks? A:

For quick and fancy GUI you can use JSF with Richfaces library. Richfaces UI components are easy to use and handy references available with code demonstration in the demo site. Probably later when your site has more data to handle and lot of information has to be transacted in database you can plug any database access framework (ORM) with it.

Q: Looking for a model that can robustly segment handwritten text lines (curved, overlapping, camera-captured images) A:

For curved and overlapping handwritten lines, I would not start with YOLO bounding boxes.

A line can have a very irregular shape, and two lines may overlap vertically, so a rectangular box can easily include parts of neighboring lines. I would look at a text-line segmentation model that predicts a pixel-level mask or a baseline/centerline instead.

For camera-captured documents, I would also add perspective correction and some augmentation for rotation, blur and uneven lighting before segmentation.

YOLO can still be useful if the lines are reasonably separated, but for heavily curved or overlapping handwriting, segmentation is probably a better fit than object detection.

Then I would pass the individual line crops/masks to TrOCR for recognition, as you suggested.
